'''Gregory Stock''' is an American [[biophysics|biophysicist]], best-selling [[author]], [[biotechnology]] [[entrepreneur]], and the former director of the Program on Medicine, Technology and Society at [[David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA|UCLA School of Medicine]]. His interests lie in the scientific and evolutionary as well as ethical, social and political implications of today's revolutions in the life sciences and in information technology and computers.

==Life, written works, and business career==

===Education===

He received an MBA from [[Harvard Business School]] in 1987, where he was a Baker Scholar and won the Freund-Porter Entrepreneurship award. Stock completed a [[doctorate]] in biophysics from [[Johns Hopkins University]] in 1977, where he received a BA and MSc in 1971.<ref>[http://socgen.ucla.edu/pmts/Stock.htm UCLA Website: Gregory Stock] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080821043849/http://socgen.ucla.edu/pmts/Stock.htm |date=2008-08-21 }}</ref>

===Biotechnology and its impact on society===

He has written extensively on the implications for society, medicine and business of the [[Human Genome Project]] and associated developments in [[molecular genetics]] and [[bioinformatics]]. The Storefront Genome,<ref>[http://www.socgen.ucla.edu/About.html The Storefront Genome] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100706075214/http://www.socgen.ucla.edu/About.html |date=2010-07-06 }}</ref> the symposium he convened in January 2003 to consider the broad challenges that cheap, easy access to our genetic constitutions drew wide media attention, and his 1998 look at the possibilities of manipulating the genetics of human embryos, the first major public discussion of this issue among distinguished scientists, opened a global debate on this then taboo topic.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Stock|first=Gregory|date=2004-07-06|title=From Regenerative Medicine to Human Design: What Are We Really Afraid Of?|url=http://www.liebertonline.com/doi/abs/10.1089/104454903770946656?cookieSet=1&journalCode=dna|journal=DNA and Cell Biology|language=en|volume=22|issue=11|pages=679–683|doi=10.1089/104454903770946656|pmid=14659040 }}</ref>

===Biotechnology entrepreneur===
Stock was the CEO of [[Signum Biosciences]].<ref>[http://www.signumbiosciences.com/about_signum.html Signum Biosciences] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090321071610/http://www.signumbiosciences.com/about_signum.html |date=2009-03-21 }}</ref> Signum Biosciences is a private biotechnology company dedicated to developing small-molecule therapeutics derived from its Signal Transduction Modulation (STM) platform to modulate signal transduction imbalances. Through research on protein networks that control biological systems, Signum is developing therapeutic candidates for [[Alzheimer's disease]], [[Parkinson's]], [[diabetes]], [[asthma]] and certain skin conditions. Signum’s STM technology provides many opportunities for the development of novel consumer products and pharmaceutical candidates. Signum was founded on the science derived from basic research studying cellular signaling at the [[Princeton University]] laboratory of [https://web.archive.org/web/20130715160210/http://www.molbio.princeton.edu/index.php?option=content&task=view&id=240 Dr. Jeffry Stock]

He sits on the editorial board of the ''[[American Journal of Bioethics]]'' and is in the department of Pediatrics at the UCLA School of Medicine.<ref>[http://www.ess.ucla.edu/huge/gregory.html UCLA Center for Society and Genetics] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090418204614/http://www.ess.ucla.edu/huge/gregory.html |date=2009-04-18 }}</ref> He is a member of the Board of Directors of Napo Pharmaceuticals, a pharmaceutical company headquartered in [[San Francisco]].<ref>[http://www.napopharma.com/people/Gregory_Stock_bd.html Napo Pharmaceuticals] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110215085914/http://www.napopharma.com/people/Gregory_Stock_bd.html |date=2011-02-15 }}</ref> He sits on the California Advisory Committee on Stem Cells and Reproductive Cloning and serves as the associate director for the Bioagenda Institute and the Center for Life Science Studies at the [[University of California at Berkeley]].

Dr. Stock has been an invited speaker to many academic, government and business conferences. He makes regular appearances on television and radio, and has appeared on [[CNN]], [[Public Broadcasting Service|PBS]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.pbs.org/wnet/religionandethics/week1051/interview2.html|title=August 17, 2007 ~ Gregory Stock {{!}} August 17, 2007 {{!}} Religion & Ethics NewsWeekly {{!}} PBS|date=2007-08-17|work=Religion & Ethics NewsWeekly|access-date=2018-03-23|language=en-US}}</ref> [[NPR]] and the [[BBC]] in shows including [[Talk of the Nation]], [[Charlie Rose]],<ref>[http://www.charlierose.com/guest/view/2294 Gregory Stock on Charlie Rose] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120221123222/http://www.charlierose.com/guest/view/2294 |date=2012-02-21 }}</ref> [[Oprah Winfrey]], Biotech Nation and [[Larry King]].

==Public policy and activities==

Stock was an early force in considering the implications of [[Human Germline Engineering|human germline engineering]] and human enhancement. Through the Program on Medicine, Technology and Society, which he founded at the UCLA School of Medicine, he organized an influential 1998 conference at [[UCLA]]: "Engineering the Human Germline," which included a panel of [[James D. Watson|James Watson]], [[French Anderson]], [[Lee Hood]] and other major figures in the life sciences. The event, which attracted considerable media attention and opened up broad debate on what was then a largely taboo topic, was covered on the front page of the [[New York Times]].<ref>Gina Kolata for the New York Times. March 21, 1998 [https://www.nytimes.com/1998/03/21/us/scientists-brace-for-changes-in-path-of-human-evolution.html?pagewanted=all&src=pm Scientists Brace for Changes In Path of Human Evolution]</ref> Through another seminal UCLA conference, Milestones on Aging, he organized, Stock helped legitimize research to significantly extend human longevity.<ref>[http://www.agingresearch.org/content/article?page=6 Alliance for Aging Research] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081126232044/http://www.agingresearch.org/content/article?page=6 |date=2008-11-26 }}</ref>  The 
event led to a follow conference he co-hosted at [[University of California, Berkeley|UC Berkeley]] with Bruce Ames and Aubrey de Grey, who went on to found the [[Methuselah Foundation]], an organization that has aggressively promoted research on life extension. The activity of the MTS Program was also critical in establishing UCLA’s Center on Society and Genetics, which actively explores broad policy issues in the genomics arena.

Stock is now primarily engaged in the development of new therapeutics at [[Signum Biosciences]], a biotech company he co-founded in 2003, but he remains active in the policy arena through UCLA's MTS Program, which he still directs, and the BioAgenda Institute,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bioagendaprograms.com/|title=BioAgenda|website=www.bioagendaprograms.com|access-date=2018-03-23}}</ref> which he is the associate director of, and through various public appearances and debates. Stock has presented diverse keynotes ranging from “The Coming Era of Personalized Medicine” at [[Medco Health Solutions|Medco]], “Trends in Health, Science and Nutrition” at the [[American Dietetic Association]], "The Future of Genomics and Healthcare" at [[Johnson and Johnson]], "The Coming Healthcare Revolution" at HIMS (Healthcare Information Management Society) and "The Evolution of the Biotech Revolution" at [[Applied Biosystems]] to "21st Century Opportunities and Challenges" at the [[World Future Society]], "Beauty, Health and Biotech: A Look Ahead" at [[Fashion Group International]], "Redesigning Humans: Best Hope, Worst Fear" at the TED (Technology, Education and Design) Conference, and "From Pharmacogenomics to Genetic Design" at the [[World Transhumanist Association]]. He has also been involved with broadcast media through guest appearances on shows such as the [[Public Broadcasting Service|PBS]] documentary "Religion and Ethics: The Challenge and Ethics of Strong Biotechnology," debates on NPR's Talk of the Nation and Charlie Rose, via an online multimedia documentary he produced with funding from the Greenwall and Sloan Foundations entitled "Human Germline Engineering: Implications for Science and Society"(www.germline.ucla.edu), and in an ARTE documentary examining key figures in Biotechnology.<ref>[http://www.ess.ucla.edu/huge/report.html Engineering the Human Germline Symposium] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080513230801/http://www.ess.ucla.edu/huge/report.html |date=2008-05-13 }}</ref> 

Stock's expertise in biotechnology, genetics and public policy in the life sciences led to his appointment on the California Advisory Committee on Stem Cells and Reproductive Cloning, Dept. of Health Services, [[State of California]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cdph.ca.gov/services/boards/HSCR/Pages/default.aspx |title=Human Stem Cell Research Advisory Committee Information |access-date=2009-05-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090528084218/http://www.cdph.ca.gov/services/boards/HSCR/Pages/default.aspx |archive-date=2009-05-28 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Debates==

Stock has always been a strong advocate for the aggressive implementation of new technology in the life sciences and he has publicly debated many leading figures in the bioethics community, including [[Francis Fukuyama]], [[Jeremy Rifkin]], [[Leon Kass]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=1141610|title=Biotechnology|work=NPR.org|access-date=2018-03-23|language=en}}</ref> [[George Annas]], [[Dan Callahan]],<ref>[http://video.google.com/videoplay?docid=-8994837371721694774 Edmonton Aging Symposium Presentation]</ref> [[Bill McKibben]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.scienceblog.com/community/older/2003/C/2003552.html|title=New website features live webcast with Dr. Gregory Stock and Bill McKibben|website=www.scienceblog.com|access-date=2018-03-23}}</ref> [[Michael Sandel]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://humanitas.org/resources/articles/articlesindex.htm#The%20Case%20Against%20Perfection|title=Resources -- Articles|website=humanitas.org|access-date=2018-03-23}}</ref> [[William B. Hurlbut|William Hurlbut]] and Nigel Cameron.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20071016081717/http://davidewingduncan.net/bioAgenda.htm The BioAgenda 2007 Great Debate: Should the world permanently ban the genetic manipulation of human embryos – yes or no?]</ref> In these appearances, he has consistently argued against restrictions on life science research including funding bans on stem cell research, moratoriums on cloning, overly protective pharmaceutical regulatory controls, and efforts to constrain anti-aging research. A fellow of the World Technology Council and [[World Academy of Art and Science]], Stock's argues in favor of the positive benefits of new technology has on human life and the role it will play on our future.

==Books==

<!-- Deleted image removed: [[Image:ThebookofQuestions.gif|right|thumb|''[[The Book of Questions]]'', by Dr.Gregory Stock.]] -->


Stock has written works on the impact and significance of recent advances in technology and the life sciences, and several bestsellers on values and ethics. His Book of Questions series, which consists of four eclectic collections of provocative situational dilemmas, was designed to generate discussion and thought about value-laden issues. The series has sold more than three million copies in total, been translated into 17 languages, and spawned a host of imitations.

His books on technology, public policy and future human evolution are:

*''[[Metaman]]:The Merging of Humans and Machines into a Global Superorganism.''(1993).
*''Engineering the Human Germline: An Exploration of the Science and Ethics of Altering the Genes We Pass to Our Children'' (2000, Oxford University Press) (Co-editor with John Campbell).
*''Redesigning Humans: Our Inevitable Genetic Future'' (2002){{pb}}''Redesigning Humans'' won the Kistler Award [[Kistler Prize]] for science writing. Stock has also written numerous articles and papers on these topics.
*''The Book of Questions'' (1987)  {{ISBN|978-0-89480-320-8}} [https://web.archive.org/web/20051203012747/http://research.arc2.ucla.edu/pmts/books.htm]
*''Business, Politics, and Ethics: The Book of Questions'' (1991, Workman. NY.)
*''Love and Sex: The Book of Questions.'' (1989, Workman. NY.)
*''The Kids' Book of Questions.'' (1988, Workman. NY.)

Stock currently serves on the editorial Board of Rejuvination Science, the International Journal of Bioethics,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ethicsandmedicine.com|title=Ethics & Medicine – International Journal of Bioethics|website=www.ethicsandmedicine.com|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-23}}</ref> the [[Journal of Evolution and Technology]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.jetpress.org/editorialboard.htm|title=JET Editorial Board|website=www.jetpress.org|access-date=2018-03-23}}</ref> and the [[American Journal of Bioethics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bioethics.net/journal/|title=Journal Backs Verification of Cloning Work in Wake of Scandal {{!}} Bioethics.net|website=www.bioethics.net|language=en|access-date=2018-03-23}}</ref>
